title: Barclays says it will cut about 5,000 jobs, citing AI efficiency
dek: A large bank links a headcount cut to AI in the same release as a profit rise. The figures come from the bank's own account as reported by outlets.
what: On Thursday 22 October Sky News posted a breaking alert that Barclays is cutting 5,000 jobs in an efficiency drive led by AI.

Yahoo Finance UK reports that Barclays will remove about 5,000 positions, roughly 5% of its global workforce, by the end of 2026. It quotes the bank describing 'organisational simplification and technology change efficiency driven by AI'. It reports that about 60% of the losses are in support functions, including fewer developers because, in the bank's words, AI makes its people more productive.

The announcement came with third quarter results. Yahoo reports net profit of £1.65 billion, up 13% on a year earlier, and group income up 3% to £7.37 billion. It quotes chief executive C. S. Venkatakrishnan citing momentum in operational and financial performance.
I read the bank's account only through press reports. I did not open the Barclays results statement, so the timing and the split by function are as those reports give them.
why: Cuts that a company ties to AI, announced beside rising profit, are being read as an early sign of what AI does to white-collar jobs. The alert repeats the bank's framing.
next: The Barclays results statement and any detail on where the cuts fall.

sources.label: Yahoo Finance UK: Barclays bank to cut about 5,000 jobs amid AI drive
